newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SCHILLING GETS $15.45 MILLION GUARANTEED EXTENSION.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SCHILLING GETS $15.45 MILLION GUARANTEED EXTENSION.

text.p: Curt Schilling agreed to a guaranteed $15.45 million contract extension with the Philadelphia Phillies Thursday, a day after his agent said the right-hander would become a free agent at the end of the season.

The contract includes three guaranteed years at $15.45 million plus an option for 2001 worth $6.5 million. The option becomes vested if Schilling, 30, pitches 450 innings in the three previous seasons (1998-2000). He is scheduled to make $3.5 million this season.

The contract also contains a no-trade clause and several award bonuses, including $150,000 for winning the Cy Young Award, $100,000 for winning the Most Valuable Player Award and $50,000 for making the All-Star team.
"We are extremely happy to have one of the premier pitchers in the game for five years," said Phillies president Bill Giles.

"We feel he will be the kingpin of our pitching staff for the next five years, and as we build to bring another championship to Philadelphia, we anticipate Curt will be a big part of reaching that goal."
Schilling attempted to work out a long-term deal with the Phillies throughout spring training and was the subject of persistent trade rumours.
Schilling was outstanding in his Opening Day start against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Tuesday, allowing just two infield hits while striking out 11 over eight innings in a 3-0 win.

Schilling and agent Jeff Borris held a conference call Wednesday with Giles and general manager Lee Thomas, but the two sides could not reach an agreement. Borris said afterward his client would become a free agent.

Schilling was 9-10 with a 3.19 ERA in 26 games last season. His best season was 1993, when he was 16-7 with a 4.02 ERA and was named Most Valuable Player of the National League Championship Series against the Atlanta Braves.
Schilling has a career record of 53-52 with Baltimore, Houston and Philadelphia. He was used primarily in the bullpen before being converted to a starter by the Phillies in 1992.
